name: Rhodes
tagline: A knights' walled city in the Aegean sun
summary: Rhodes Town wraps one of Europe's best-preserved medieval cities, built by the Knights of St John, inside massive walls. Beyond it the island has beaches, the white village of Lindos below its acropolis, and boats to nearby Symi.
seasonNote: May, June, September and October are ideal. July and August are hot and crowded. In winter many hotels close.
arrival: Rhodes Airport is 25 minutes from town. Flights come from Athens (1 hour) and many European cities in summer; ferries run from Piraeus (about 13 hours) and nearby islands.
gettingAround: The old town is car-free; buses run to Lindos and beaches, or rent a car or scooter.
cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; keep cash for small tavernas and beach sunbeds.
foodTip: Grilled fish, souvlaki, Greek salad with island cheese, and pitaroudia chickpea fritters.
buyTip: Local honey, olive-oil soap, ceramics from Lindos and leather sandals.
baseArea: Inside the old town walls or near Mandraki

connections.note: Long ferries also run from Piraeus.
Seasonal; or a ferry to Marmaris in Türkiye.
